data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the syllable "Om" is considered to be the sacred sound of the universe and the embodiment of the divine consciousness. It is believed to have spiritual power and can be used to focus the mind, purify the thoughts, and connect with the divine. While the name "Omav" itself may not hold spiritual significance, the use of the letter "Om" in the name is a reminder of the spiritual power and significance of that sound in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Om is the primal sound of the universe, representing the divine consciousness that underlies all existence. Av is a symbol of Shakti, the divine feminine energy, embodied in the goddesses Parvati and Saraswati. Together, Om-Av signifies the union of consciousness and energy, the eternal dance of creation and dissolution.

historical_references.reference: According to the 'Skanda Purana', a Hindu mythological text, the name 'Omav' is considered a synonym for the sacred syllable 'Om'. It is believed that the recitation of the syllable 'Om' invokes the divine presence of various deities and brings peace and prosperity. The 'Skanda Purana' is believed to have been written between the 6th and 8th centuries AD.

The name 'Omav' is also mentioned in the 'Mahabharata', one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. 'Omav' is the name of the wife of the king Bhishma Pitamaha, who is revered as the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty. The 'Mahabharata' is believed to have been composed between the 4th and 2nd centuries BC.
